related_questions.question: Are the new COVID tests available?
related_questions.snippet: These at-home OTC COVID-19 diagnostic tests are FDA authorized for self-testing at home (or in other locations) without a prescription. Tests are available online or at local stores and you collect your own sample, perform the test, and read the result yourself without the need to send a sample to a laboratory.
related_questions.title: At-Home OTC COVID-19 Diagnostic Tests - FDA

related_questions.question: Can you buy COVID tests anymore?
related_questions.snippet: They are available for free on the NHS to people who are eligible for COVID-19 treatment. Information: If you want to get tested, but you're not eligible for COVID-19 treatment, you'll need to pay for the test yourself. You can buy COVID-19 rapid lateral flow tests from some pharmacies and retailers.
related_questions.title: COVID-19 rapid lateral flow test - NHS

related_questions.question: Are there tests for the new strain of COVID?
related_questions.snippet: Research suggests that in general, antigen tests do a good job of picking up a variety of COVID-19 variants.
related_questions.title: COVID tests: Do at-home tests work on newer variants? - Harvard Health

related_questions.question: Which COVID test takes the longest?
related_questions.snippet: Molecular tests are generally more accurate and mostly processed in a laboratory, which takes longer; antigen tests—or “rapid tests”—are processed pretty much anywhere, including at home, in doctors' offices, or in pharmacies. You can get antigen test results in about 15 minutes, but they tend to be less accurate.
